**Market Parameters Report – July 2009** 





### **1. Demand for platinum** 

- _We have downgraded our estimates of platinum demand in 2010 in anticipation of a subdued recovery in autocatalyst (from the 2009 low) and moderated capital spending on capacity expansions in the glass sector.  Meanwhile, our estimates of demand in 2009 and our forecast for 2011 remain broadly unchanged._ 

|**Platinum 000 ozs**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Autocatalyst|3,814|2,885|2,987|3,427|
|Jewellery|1,646|2,092|2,231|2,411|
|_Chemical_|346|307|303|389|
|_Electronics_|378|320|326|343|
|_Glass_|441|95|204|468|
|_Petroleum_|200|225|298|242|
|_Retail investment_|452|390|195|115|
|_Other_|461|426|459|510|
|Industrial|2,279|1,763|1,785|2,067|
|**Total**|**7,739**|**6,740**|**7,003**|**7,904**|



### **1.1  Autocatalyst** 

- Our assumptions for autocatalyst demand now assume a 20% decline in global light vehicle production in 2009 with improvements of 9% and 13% in 2010 and 2011 respectively.  As before, the bulk of the damage in 2009 is in the developed economies of North America, Europe and Japan where, in addition, production volumes of heavy duty vehicles is expected to fall by 40%.  China is the only market likely to post significant production growth in 2009. 

- Although platinum is benefiting from increased DPF fitment (especially in Europe ahead of Euro 5 regulations from September 2009), it faces continuing headwinds from substitution in gasoline and most notably nowadays in diesel applications where the use of bi‐metallic platinum/palladium catalysts is increasing.  The effects of this are unlikely to be overcome by market share gains and we expect diesel penetration to remain static at around 25% of global light vehicle productio

n over the forecast period. 

### **1.2 Jewellery** (reported as gross fabrication) 

- Platinum prices have struggled to gain traction above $1,200.  We see this as positive for jewellery demand in China this year and have upgraded our demand estimates accordingly. For 2010 and 2011 we remain of the view that benign platinum prices will prevail, providing continued support for healthy demand growth in China, with demand elsewhere subdued. 

### **1.3 Industrial & other applications** 

- We have lowered our demand estimates for the use of platinum in glass applications. Demand for LCD glass substrates rebounded strongly in Q2 and the outlook among panel makers has turned sharply positive for the remainder of 2009.  However, the glass makers are responding to this sudden upturn by re‐commissioning capacity they were forced to idle in late 2008/early 2009 and remain cautious towards expansions in 2010.  Similarly, capacity expansions in fibreglass have been deferred into 2011.

### **2. Demand for palladium** 

- _Based on a slower recovery in global auto production, we have lowered our demand estimate for palladium in 2010.  Our forecasts for 2009 and 2011 are broadly unchanged._ 

|**Palladium 000 ozs**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Autocatalyst|4,408|3,484|3,983|4,580|
|Jewellery|1,301|1,484|1,606|1,691|
|_Dental_|776|742|730|717|

|_Retail investment_|84|170|85|58|
|_Other_|91|76|86|93|
|Industrial|2,683|2,453|2,522|2,703|
|**Total**|**8,391**|**7,421**|**8,111**|**8,974**|



### **2.1 Autocatalyst** 

- Although we have lowered our demand estimates, we remain of the view that palladium will recover more rapidly than platinum in this sector.  Whilst demand for both metals is driven mainly by vehicle volumes, palladium’s advantage is in substitution (most notably in diesel applications) and stronger production gains from next year in gasoline fuelled vehicles where palladium is dominant. 

### **2.2 Jewellery** (reported as gross fabrication) 

- We have made a moderate upgrade to our forecasts of palladium jewellery demand.  This is based on a more positive view of demand in China and the continuing (albeit slow) development of the market in the US and in Europe, where the UK recently included palladium in its hallmarking system. 

### **2.3 Industrial** 

- Our forecasts in these areas are unchanged pending a major review scheduled for August. The results of this will be included in our next report but are unlikely to be radically altered from the levels reported above.

### **3. Supply** 

### **3.1  Platinum supply** 

- _We have scaled back our estimates for supply growth from South Africa in 2010 and 2011. These adjustments are provisional pending a major review of mine production and supply from recycling scheduled for Au

gust._ 

|**Platinum 000 ozs**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**Mineproduction:**|||||
|South Africa|4,671|4,655|4,800|5,000|
|Russia|835|799|792|786|
|Canada|227|201|268|276|
|United States|115|107|92|80|
|Zimbabwe|180|195|222|240|
|Others|123|112|109|109|
|**Total mineproduction**|**6,151**|**6,069**|**6,283**|**6,492**|
|Autocatalyst recycling|998|883|1,075|1,174|
|Jewelleryscrap|910|299|281|264|
|**Total supply**|**8,059**|**7,250**|**7,640**|**7,929**|



- We remain of the view that platinum mine production in South Africa will stabilise in 2009 but we are less convinced over the prospects for growth in 2010 and 2011.  It now seems likely that Anglo Platinum will cut production later this year at marginal shafts on its Rustenburg property.  Furthermore, they are now targeting zero growth in overall refined platinum production (including purchased concentrates) through to 2011, absent a recovery in demand.  We think the reality is unlikely to be quite as harsh as the rhetoric suggests but have eased back our growth estimates for South Africa none‐the‐less. 

- Although there are some signs of a recovery in autocatalyst recycling volumes, it remains likely that recovery of both palladium and platinum will decline in 2009 for the first time ever.  While lower steel and PGM prices have played a role in slowing the flow of material from breakers yards, it seems that the downturn in new vehicle sales is having an increasingly pronounced effect at the opposite end of the food chain.  Until recently, the effect of this was masked by the elevated commodity prices through to the middle of 2008. 

- Our estimates for jewellery scrap recycling are unchanged.  Together with autocatalyst recycling, this will be reviewed in detail during August.

### **4. Market balances** 

### **4.1 Platinum** 

- _We remain of the view that platinum will register a substantial gross surplus in 2009 and 2010.  Thereafter, with demand recovering strongly and lower estimates for supply growth, it appears likely that the market will move close to balance at the gross level in 2011._ 

- _We have raised our estimates for net investment in ETFs in 2009 and retained our earlier forecasts for 2010 and 2011.  As a result, platinum appears likely to register a moderate residual deficit in 2011.  However, this will be overshadowed by the surpluses we now forecast for 2009 and 2010 at both the gross and residual level._ 

|**Platinum 000 ozs**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|New supply|8,059|7,250|7,640|7,929|
|Fabrication demand|7,739|6,740|7,003|7,904|
|**_Gross surplus(deficit)_**|**320**|**510**|**637**|**25**|
|ETF demand|(102)|(280)|(160)|(120)|
|**Residual surplus(deficit)**|**217**|**230**|**477**|**(95)**|



### **4.2 Palladium** 

- _Despite the various adjustments to supply and demand the picture for palladium is little changed.   We expect a sharp contraction in the gross deficit in 2009 as the fall in demand outpaces the reduction in supply.  After a balanced market this year, we expect a return to gross deficit from 2010 with a substantial short‐fall of new supply in 2011._ 

- _However, with Russian stock sales expected to continue, and despite positive inflows to ETFs, palladium is likely to remain over‐supplied at the residual level until the emergence of a moderate deficit in 2011.  This is predicated on the view that sales of palladium by Russia’s state agencies (in other words, from inventory) will ease over the forecast period._

### **5. Above‐ground stocks** 

- _Above‐ground stocks are implied from historical trade data for Switzerland (dating from 1970) and declared stocks on the Nymex and Tocom futures exchanges.  Excluded are stocks held by governments (including Russia), producers, refiners and fabricators and consumers._ 

|**Implied stocks**|**2008**|**2009F**|**2010F**|**2011F**|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**Platinum:**|||||
|Stock atyear end(million ozs)|1.86|2.37|3.01|3.03|
|Demand cover(months)|2.9|4.2|5.1|4.6|
|**Palladium:**|||||
|Stock atyear end(million ozs)|7.67|8.94|9.49|9.47|
|Demand cover(months)|11.0|14.5|14.0|12.7|



- Over the next three years platinum’s demand cover is expected to rise from around three months to approaching five months as its gross surplus persists in 2009 and 2010.

- For palladium, above‐ground stocks are forecast to remain substantial over the forecast period at more than one year’s demand cover.  Although gross deficits from 2010 create downward pressure, this will be more than offset by continuing inflows of palladium from Russian state stocks into Swiss vaults. 

- _Note: forecast sales of palladium from Russian state stocks have now been included as inflows to implied above‐ground stocks in Switzerland.  These inclusions serve to inflate stocks in Switzerland but are balanced by commensurate declines in Russia’s state owned inventories._

### **6. Prices and related indicators** 

### **6.1 Platinum** 

_After failing to make $1,300, platinum has become compressed in a relatively narrow range between $1,100 and $1,200 and volatility has subsided accordingly.  Platinum is receiving little impetus from its own fundamentals and is a slave to gold and the dollar._ 



_Technically motivated traders will have seen little in platinum’s RSI to motivate action in July in either direction. With volatility subdued, the RSI appears firmly in neutral._ 



_The 50 and 200 day MAs suggest platinum’s momentum has dissipated, indicating that its chances of consolidating on any breaks above $1,200 may be slim (particularly as Chinese jewellery buyers are likely to pull the plug at this level)._ 



Page | 7 

**Market Parameters Report – July 2009** 





### **6.2 Palladium** 

_Palladium is showing some resilience above $250 but continues to take it cues from platinum (and in turn gold). Consequently, palladium’s volatility has behaved in a similar fashion.  In other words, it’s collapsed._ 

_Over recent weeks, palladium’s strengthening RSI may have served as a sell signal but attracted limited action; a good sign and one reason we have described palladium as resilient. Having survived that, it will hardly be worried by the neutral scores now being recorded._ 

_Palladium’s profile in terms of its MA’s looks similar to platinum.  However, with spot remaining at or above the 50 day over recent weeks (unlike platinum), this could be regarded as mildly positive by some.  On the whole,(and regardless of the charts) there is more warmth towards palladium right now._
